literature_notes: All four ledger lines describe C-terminally tagged full-length AMN constructs (L1/L2: five c-myc tags; L3: mycDDK from OriGene; L4: GFP-tagged). AMN is a type I single-pass membrane protein with its C-terminus in the intracellular domain (residues 384–453), so every confirmed C-terminal tag faces the cytoplasm and cannot serve as an extracellular surface tag. L4 ('GFP-tagged amnionless') names neither N- nor C-terminus; because AMN has one extracellular terminus (mature N-terminus, residue 20) AND one intracellular terminus (residue 453), the topology_derived rule — which requires exactly one extracellular terminus to resolve the position — does not apply, and the GFP site cannot be pinned to the extracellular face. No ledger line reports a tag insertion at any extracellular position of AMN or a close ortholog. Zero qualifying surface sites.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal c-myc tag (five copies) on full-length human AMN expressed in mammalian cells; C-terminus falls in the intracellular domain (residues 384–453), confirmed functional for studying endocytic signals.
C-terminal mycDDK tag on full-length human AMN (OriGene plasmid) used in flow-cytometry expression studies; same intracellular C-terminus.
